Important Points

  • These custom fields will appear in the access request form for SAP Concur
  • All four fields are mandatory for both new and existing users
  • Values must be provided in the correct format, otherwise provisioning will fail

Even though SAP IAG provides an option to edit or deactivate these fields under Custom Fields, it is recommended not to change them, as they are required for Concur provisioning.

 

Additional Note

SAP is introducing additional custom fields to support more Concur attributes. You can track updates here: SAP Roadmap Explorer – SAP IAG Concur Enhancements

 

Step 5: Run Repository Sync Job

This step helps to synchronize users and access (roles/profiles) from SAP Concur into SAP IAG for governance processes.

After creating the application, run the Repository Sync job to fetch data from SAP Concur.

Navigate to Administration → Job Scheduler and execute the Repository Sync job for the SAP Concur application

Once the job is completed successfully, user and access data from SAP Concur are synchronized to SAP IAG.

You can verify the synchronized data in:

  • Maintain User Data
  • Access Maintenance (use filters for SAP Concur)

User Data

  • SAP Concur user ID is displayed in the format: <user_id>@<CompanyEntityCode>
  • The <user_id> corresponds to the login name maintained in SAP CIS

Access Data

Under Access Maintenance, two types of access are available for SAP Concur:

  1. Concur Product: Represents Concur profiles such as Expense, Invoice, Reporting, Request, and Travel
  2. Single Roles: Represents authorization roles such as EXP_APPROVER, EXP_ATTENDEE_ADMIN, EXP_CONFIG_ADMIN_CLIENT, etc.

Both access types can be requested via SAP IAG. Additional attributes such as: Business Process, Subprocess, Criticality, Alias, Assignment Approvers etc. can be maintained to control workflow routing and approval determination.

Note:
Only users assigned with the IAG_RAA_DEFAULT group are available for role assignment approval.

 

Step 6: Configure Access Risk Ruleset

This step helps to enable risk analysis by importing and activating SAP Concur-specific segregation of duties rules.

For risk analysis, the standard GLOBAL ruleset for SAP Concur needs to be requested.

  • Create an SAP Support case for component: GRC-IAG-AA (Access Analysis Service)
  • Provide required access (IAS Administration) to SAP to upload the ruleset

Once the ruleset is uploaded:

  • A business function group SAP_CONCUR is created
  • All SAP Concur-related risks are available under this group

Ruleset Behavior

  • SAP Concur roles are standard and cannot be customized
  • Risks are defined based on conflicting role combinations

Example:

Post ruleset setup, validate the risk count against the business function group and run the Access Analysis job from the Job Scheduler.

After completion of Access Analysis job User-level risks can be checked in ‘Access Analysis’ application and role-level risks can be checked in ‘Access Maintenance’ application.

             

Step 7: User ID mapping

This step aligns user identities across systems to avoid duplicates and ensure accurate license consumption.

User ID mapping is important for license optimization in SAP IAG. The Monitored User List in Maintain User Data shows users consuming IAG licenses

Key Consideration

SAP Concur uses a different user ID format: <user_ID>@<prefix>

If multiple applications are integrated with SAP IAG:

  • The same user may appear as different users due to different ID formats
  • This can lead to duplicate license consumption

SAP IAG supports auto user ID mapping for most applications Refer: SAP Note 3553352 (Auto-Generated Entries in User ID Mapping) however, SAP Concur is not supported for auto-mapping

Hence to avoid duplicate license consumption user ID mapping must be maintained manually. This requires additional monitoring as part of ongoing operations for new user creation and also increases administrative effort.

 

How to Maintain Mapping

  • Navigate to: Administration → Maintain User ID Mapping
  • Mapping can be maintained: Individually or via Bulk upload through CSV file
  • Master User ID → Login name from user source and Mapped ID → SAP Concur User ID

 

Additional Notes

  • Other IAG services (Access Request, Workflow, Role Design, Access Analysis, Access Certification) work similarly to other applications
  • Privileged Access Management (PAM) Service is not supported for SAP Concur

 

Key Learnings and Limitations

Based on implementation experience, below are some important points to be aware of:

1. Provisioning Behavior (Asynchronous Processing)

Provisioning in SAP Concur works in an asynchronous manner.

  • Step 1: When the access request is submitted, the first run of the provisioning job shows the status as “In Process”
  • Step 2: In the next job run, the final status is updated as “Successful” or “Failed” based on the actual result

So, the provisioning result is not available immediately in the first run.

2. Manual User ID Mapping Required

As SAP Concur does not support automated user ID mapping:

  • Manual mapping is required in SAP IAG
  • Continuous monitoring is needed for new users

Without this, duplicate users may be created, leading to additional license consumption.

3. Mandatory Custom Fields

All four custom fields are mandatory:

  • COUNTRY
  • LOCALE
  • REIMBURSEMENT_CURRENCY
  • REIMBURSEMENT_TYPE

If any field is left empty or deactivated, provisioning will fail.

4. No Validation for Custom Fields

Custom fields accept only specific values (mentioned in step 4) and formats (case-sensitive).

However:

  • Validation is not enforced at the request submission stage, which may require additional checks during provisioning
  • Users can submit incorrect values
  • Request goes through full approval workflow
  • Failure happens only during provisioning job execution.

In addition:

  • Logs may require additional analysis to identify the exact issue
  • Administrators need to analyze logs to find the problem

 5. No Pre-population of Custom Fields

  • Custom fields need to be maintained for both new and existing users
  • There is no pre-filled data even for existing users

This requires proper end-user training before rollout.

 6. Partial User Creation in case of errors

If incorrect values are provided in custom fields user may still get created in SAP Concur but no profiles or roles are assigned

Such users are difficult to find using standard user search and may require support from SAP Concur functional team to verify at database level.

Users who exist in SAP Concur but do not have any profiles (Expense, Travel, etc.) will still appear in Maintain User Data and will be counted for SAP IAG licensing.

7. No Bulk Provisioning Support

SAP IAG currently does not support bulk user provisioning/deprovisioning for SAP Concur.

Recommended approach:

  • Use SAP ICS (Integration with SAP Concur Solutions) / SAP IPS for user creation with basic roles and/or user account termination/deactivation.
  • Use SAP IAG only for role-based access requests

8. Option for HR-Driven Provisioning

Integration with SuccessFactors can be used to trigger user creation/termination and manage lifecycle and provisioning automatically.

9. Refresh Token Handling

  • Refresh token used in BTP destination has a validity of 6 months
  • SAP IAG / SAP IPS automatically refreshes the token during provisioning job execution

No manual intervention is required in normal scenarios.

10. Standard Risk Rules May Need Adjustment

The Global ruleset for SAP Concur includes some risks which may not be relevant because SAP Concur has built-in controls for certain scenarios to prevent risks.

Such risks can be reviewed with business and deactivated, if required.

 

Overall, the integration is manageable, but attention to detail is important, especially around custom fields and user mapping. This guidance is based on practical implementation experience, highlighting what worked well and the challenges encountered during execution.

Going forward, SAP may address some of these challenges, such as improvements in custom field handling, automated user ID mapping, more relevant global rulesets, and clearer provisioning logs, which should simplify the integration further.

If you have faced similar challenges or have additional insights, feel free to share your experience in the comments.

entry.title: Automating Time-Bound SAP SuccessFactors RBP Access with Entra ID and Cloud Identity Services
entry.content:
Introduction

What if an HR administrator needs elevated access to SAP SuccessFactors for two weeks? Or an AMS support team member needs temporary access to troubleshoot an issue for an approved support period?

In both cases, access should be approved, time-bound and automatically removed when it is no longer required.

Traditionally, this may involve manually adding users to SuccessFactors Permission Groups and remembering to remove them later. This creates administrative effort and increases the risk of temporary access remaining active longer than intended.

A better approach is to use Microsoft Entra ID for access governance, while continuing to use SuccessFactors Role-Based Permissions (RBP) to control application access. By connecting Microsoft Entra ID with SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication (IAS) and Identity Provisioning (IPS), approved group memberships can be provisioned to SuccessFactors Permission Groups automatically.

From Project Experience to Practical Guidance

In a recent SuccessFactors project, I implemented this approach using Microsoft Entra ID and SAP Cloud Identity Services (IAS/IPS). It provided an opportunity to work through the complete lifecycle of time-bound SuccessFactors access and see how it can be applied in a real-world implementation.

In this blog, I share the solution approach, key configuration steps and some important implementation considerations.

Note on Microsoft Entra ID Governance

An Entra ID specialist or IAM Engineer is required to configure Access Packages, approval workflows and time-bound access policies in Microsoft Entra ID. The configuration of Entra ID Governance is outside the scope of this blog. This blog focuses on how the configured Entra ID Governance capabilities integrate with SAP Cloud Identity Services and SAP SuccessFactors to enable controlled, time-bound access.

Solution Overview

The solution follows this flow:

Microsoft Entra ID manages who can request access, approval and duration. IAS and IPS handle the identity and group provisioning, while SuccessFactors RBP determines what the user can access.

Prerequisites

Before starting the IAS, IPS and Microsoft Entra ID configuration, ensure the following are available:

  • SuccessFactors: Required RBP Permission Groups and Permission Roles are configured.
  • Cloud Identity Services: IAS is configured for SuccessFactors, and IPS is connected to the required systems.
  • Microsoft Entra ID: Required users, groups, owners and approval structure are defined.
  • Access governance: Approval process and access duration/expiry requirements are agreed.
  • Identity mapping: A consistent user identifier is available across Entra ID, IAS, IPS and SuccessFactors.
  • Access & permissions: Required admin accounts, API permissions and authorizations are available.

Step 1: Configure Microsoft Entra ID to SAP Cloud Identity Services

  • In the Identity Authentication Service (IAS) admin console, provision a new System Administrator account and generate an API Client Secret and assign the required permissions for SCIM REST API operations (READ/WRITE access for users/groups)

  • In Microsoft Entra ID, configure the Enterprise Application SAP Cloud Identity Services using SCIM protocol, targeting the IAS SCIM base URL and authenticating with the generated system credentials.

This allows Entra ID to provision user profiles and group assignment payloads directly to SAP Cloud Identity Services via SCIM.

The screenshots above are only intended to illustrate standard user provisioning from Entra ID to IAS via the SCIM API. Depending on your Entra ID tenant tier (e.g., Microsoft Entra ID P1/P2), the outbound SCIM payload can also include the groups as required for the downstream SuccessFactors transformation scenario.

Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/saas-apps/sap-cloud-platform-identity-authentication-provisioning-tutorial

Step 2: Configure IAS as the IPS Source

Next, configure IAS as the source system in IPS so that IPS can read the users and group memberships provisioned from Entra ID. For this, establish certificate-based authentication and configure Identity Authentication as the Source System.

  • Source System:
    • In IPS, create a new Source System of type Identity Authentication. Use default transformation.
    • Configure mandatory Properties
  • Authentication & Authorization:
    • Generate a certificate directly within the newly created IPS Source System
    • Download the certificate and assign it to the System Administrator account in IAS (we can use the same administrator account used by Entra ID)

Reference: https://help.sap.com/docs/identity-provisioning/identity-provisioning/identity authentication?q=source+system

Step 3: Configure SuccessFactors as the IPS Target

IPS now needs to be able to update SuccessFactors Permission Groups. For this, establish certificate-based authentication and configure SuccessFactors as the Target System.

  • Target System:
    • In IPS, create a new Target System of type SuccessFactors. Select the IAS source system created in the previous step.
    • Configure the required target properties.
  • SuccessFactors Authentication:
    • Generate a certificate directly from the newly created Target System.
    • In SuccessFactors, Security Center, X.509 Certificate Mapping, map the public certificate to an administrative service user that has permissions to access and manage Role-Based Permission and Permission Groups.

Reference: https://help.sap.com/docs/identity-provisioning/identity-provisioning/target-sap-successfactors

Step 4: Configure the IPS Transformation

The transformation is not simply passing the group membership from IAS to SuccessFactors. The user entity must first be processed by IPS so that IPS can establish the correlation between the source user and the corresponding SuccessFactors target user. Once that correlation exists, resolveEntityIds in the group transformation can resolve IAS group member to the corresponding SuccessFactors userId.

The JSON below represents the Target Transformation JSON used in IPS to map user identities and group assignments to SuccessFactors Permission Groups (Dynamic Groups)

User block:

  • condition: Ensures the transformation only processes user records containing an employeeNumber
  • skipOperations: ["delete"]: Prevents unintentional user deletions in SuccessFactors
  • userId: Maps the SCIM employeeNumber directly to the target SuccessFactors userId

  • replaceFirstString: Trims external naming conventions or internal security prefixes (e.g., SF_GRP_PREFIX_) from displayName so the group name created in SuccessFactors matches the business definition
  • resolveEntityIds: group member resolution

Reference: https://help.sap.com/docs/identity-provisioning/identity-provisioning/transformation-expressions

Step 5: Payload Validation
Upstream Group Assignment in IAS

SCIM group membership payload provisioned from Microsoft Entra ID into SAP Cloud Identity Services (IAS).

IPS Transformed User Payload

Target user transformation payload mapping the employee userId (personIdExternal).

The user transformation block must execute so IPS can execute downstream member resolution.

Outbound OData API Payload (DynamicGroup)

Transformed target JSON payload generated for the SuccessFactors DynamicGroup OData API, containing the target groupID, groupName (prefix removed), and resolved member userIds.

Verified SuccessFactors Permission Group

Admin Center view confirming the updated Role-Based Permission (RBP) Dynamic Group reflecting the synchronized Entra ID group membership.

 



Important Implementation Note: SuccessFactors User ID

By default, the SuccessFactors userId is not exposed and mapped directly in standard SAP Cloud Identity Services schemas or default SAP SuccessFactors SCIM API mappings. While employeeNumber in IAS is typically mapped from personIdExternal in SuccessFactors, relying solely on personIdExternal can create challenges in rehire scenarios, where a new userId may be generated). To address this, a separate job can be used to retrieve the SuccessFactors userId and populate it into a custom attribute in SAP Cloud Identity Services. This custom attribute can then be used in the IPS target transformation instead of employeeNumber, providing a reliable way to resolve and maintain the SuccessFactors member userId.

Reference: https://help.sap.com/docs/successfactors-platform/managing-user-information/mapping-between-scim-users-and-odata-user

In this implementation, the SuccessFactors OData API (DynamicGroup) was used to update Permission Group membership. The SuccessFactors SCIM API (Groups) can also be used and the same pattern using resolveEntityIds may be applied to translate member identities, although the target transformation will need to be adjusted to suit the SCIM target schema.

Reference: https://help.sap.com/docs/successfactors-platform/managing-user-information/overview-of-sap-successfactors-workforce-system-for-cross-domain-identity-management-api

End-to-End Testing

Once the configuration is complete, test the complete lifecycle using a test user.

1. Request Access
The user requests the required application or role through Microsoft My Apps and completes the configured approval process.

2. User Group Provisioning in IAS
Once approved, the user's membership in the relevant Entra ID group is provisioned to IAS.

The updated logs from Job Execution in IPS should show the payload sent to SuccessFactors to update the Permission Group membership.

3. User Group Assignment in SuccessFactors
 When the scheduled IPS job runs, the group membership is transformed and provisioned to the corresponding SuccessFactors Dynamic Permission Group. The user should now receive the associated RBP access.

4. Validate expiry
 When the configured access duration expires in Microsoft Entra ID, the user's group membership is removed. The subsequent provisioning cycle processes this change and removes the user from the corresponding SuccessFactors Permission Group.

This completes the access lifecycle without requiring manual removal in SuccessFactors.

 


Conclusion: The Complete Identity Lifecycle

This approach provides a reusable pattern for managing temporary SuccessFactors access through an organisation's existing identity governance framework. Microsoft Entra ID manages the request, approval and access duration, while SAP Cloud Identity Services handles the identity and group provisioning, and SuccessFactors RBP ultimately controls the user's access.

The result is a more controlled and auditable way to provision temporary SuccessFactors access without relying on manual Permission Group administration.

entry.title: Extending Case Approvals in SAP Sales & Service Cloud v2 + ESM: Using Business Roles for Multi-Users
entry.content:
This blog post is a continuation of: Assigning a Custom Party Role to a Case for Approvals in SAP Sales & Service Cloud v2 + ESM

Introduction

The previous blog post walked through how to create a Custom Party Role, add it to a Case Party Schema, and wire it into an Autoflow approval — a clean and effective pattern for routing a case to a named approver.

But what happens when your business scenario requires more than one approver? What if an entire team needs to approve a case, and that team membership changes over time?

SAP Sales & Service Cloud v2 (SSC v2) and ESM do not have a native Branch or Approval Hierarchy construct the way some other products do. There is no built-in concept of "send to a department" or "broadcast to a group approval pool." You cannot pick a Business Role directly in the Approval Rule as a recipient group — the approval framework works with individual people assigned to the case.

This extension blog describes a practical pattern to bridge that gap:

Use a Business Role in SSC v2 as the governed container of approvers. Sync its membership from IAS via IPS over SCIM. Populate a non-unique Custom Party Role on the Case with all members of that Business Role. Then use the Case Approval flow to route to all those party role members simultaneously.

The result: a fully dynamic, centrally governed multi-user approval — without needing a branch or hierarchy model.

The Problem: No Branch, No Hierarchy, But Multiple Approvers Needed

In SSC v2/ESM case approvals, the approval process resolves its recipients from people assigned to a specific party role on the case. This works well for a single approver — assign one person to the "Line Approver" party role, and the approval goes to them.

However, real-world scenarios often require:

  • A team of approvers where any one member can take action (e.g., a support management pool)
  • A scenario where all members must approve (e.g., a compliance sign-off)
  • A quorum approval (e.g., at least 2 out of 5 approvers must accept)

And critically: approval team membership changes. People join, leave, change roles. Hardcoding names in configuration is not maintainable.

The answer lies in combining three capabilities:

  1. Business Roles in SSC v2 — as a group of approvers with a meaningful identity
  2. IAS User Groups + IPS SCIM provisioning — for centralized lifecycle management of who is in that group
  3. BTP Extensibility for Assignment of Users to Case from Business Role
  4. Non-unique Custom Party Role on the Case — as the runtime carrier of multiple approvers that the approval flow reads

Architecture Overview

IAS (Identity Authentication Service)
  └── User Group: "CASE_APPROVERS_GRP1"
       ├── User A
       ├── User B
       └── User C
          │
          │  IPS SCIM Sync (Business Role provisioning)
          ▼
SSC v2 / ESM
  └── Business Role: Z_CASE_APPROVERS_GRP1
       ├── User A (assigned this Business Role)
       ├── User B (assigned this Business Role)
       └── User C (assigned this Business Role)
          │
          │  Manual or Automated Party Assignment(BTP Extension)
          ▼
  Case → Custom Party Role: Z_GRP_APPROVER (non-unique)
       ├── User A (Party on Case)
       ├── User B (Party on Case)
       └── User C (Party on Case)
          │
          │  Autoflow → Approval Action
          ▼
  Approval Tasks sent to User A, User B, User C
  (All / Any One / At Least X — configurable)

Why This Pattern Works Without a Branch or Hierarchy

ChallengeHow It's Solved
No group/branch concept in approvalsBusiness Role acts as the group container; its members are loaded into a non-unique party role on the case
Approval team changes over timeIAS group membership is updated → IPS SCIM sync propagates changes to SSC v2 Business Role → Next case uses the updated team
Different cases need different approval groupsCreate one Business Role + Custom Party Role per approval group; populate the right one on each case based on conditions
Need any-one or all-must-approve semanticsControlled by the Approval Rule setting — no process redesign needed
Hardcoded user names in configurationNo user names anywhere in config — only role/group names

Summary

This pattern extends the Custom Party Role + Autoflow approval approach with a scalable, centrally governed layer. By treating a Business Role as the approval group, syncing its members from IAS via IPS over SCIM, and surfacing them on the case through a non-unique Custom Party Role, you unlock multi-user approval semantics in SAP SSC v2 / ESM — without needing any branch, hierarchy, or hardcoded user configuration.

The result is an approval flow that is:

  • Dynamic — membership changes in IAS flow through automatically
  • Flexible — supports any-one, all-must, or quorum approval modes
  • Maintainable — no user names in process configuration
  • Governed — IAS is the single source of truth for who approves what

Related blogs:

  • Assigning a Custom Party Role to a Case for Approvals in SAP Sales & Service Cloud v2 + ESM
  • Introducing SCIM API for SAP Sales & Service Cloud v2
  • Expanding SCIM API Support for SAP Sales & Service Cloud Version 2/ESM

entry.title: Why Manually Created Users Lose their Roles After SCIM Replication in SSCv2 +ESM— And How to Fix It
entry.content:
The Situation

Identity and access management in modern enterprise environments often involves a mix of provisioning strategies. In SAP's Sales & Service Cloud v2 (SSCv2) & SAP Enterprise Service Management (ESM), it is common to find tenants where some users are created manually by administrators while others are provisioned automatically through SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management). This hybrid approach seems harmless — until you run a SCIM replication job and discover that manually created users have silently lost all of their assigned roles.

This is not a random glitch. It is a predictable, reproducible behavior rooted in how SCIM-enabled tenants manage role assignments — and understanding it is the first step to preventing it.

The Problem

In a SCIM-enabled SSCv2 tenant, users who were manually created (i.e., not provisioned through SCIM) and had business roles manually assigned to them lose those role assignments whenever a SCIM replication process runs — even though these users are not managed by SCIM at all.

What makes this particularly puzzling is that the Cloud Identity Service (CIS) logs show no record of updates to those manually created users during the replication run. From the system's perspective, nothing happened — yet the roles are gone.

How to Reproduce It

The issue is entirely reproducible. Here is the sequence of events that triggers it:

  1. Create a user manually in SSCv2 (outside of any SCIM provisioning flow).
  2. Assign one or more business roles to this user directly in SSCv2.
  3. Create a second user via SCIM provisioning from the Cloud Identity Service (CIS).
  4. Assign the same roles to the SCIM-managed user through CIS.
  5. Execute the SCIM replication process.
  6. Check the manually created user's role assignments.

Result: The manually created user's role assignments have been removed. The SCIM-managed user's assignments are intact. The CIS logs contain no trace of any action against the manually created user.

Why This Happens: The Root Cause

The behavior is not a bug in the traditional sense — it is a consequence of how role replication works in a SCIM-enabled tenant.

In SSCv2, when SCIM is enabled, the authoritative source for role assignments is Identity Authentication Service (IAS), not SSCv2 itself. The replication flow works as follows:

  • Roles are replicated from SSCv2 to IAS via replication jobs.
  • User-role assignments are replicated from IAS back to SSCv2 via those same jobs.

This means that during a replication run, SSCv2 does not selectively update only SCIM-managed users. Instead, it synchronizes role assignments based on what IAS reports. If a role is assigned to a SCIM-managed user in IAS, that assignment gets written to SSCv2. But because the manually created user has no corresponding record in IAS, the replication job effectively overwrites the role assignment state for that role — removing it from any user not represented in the IAS replication payload.

The silence in the CIS logs is explained by the same mechanism: CIS did not act on the manually created user. The removal is a side-effect of the IAS-driven synchronization overwriting what SSCv2 holds locally.

The Fix: Make Manually Created Users SCIM-Managed

The resolution is straightforward once the root cause is understood: manually created users need to become SCIM-managed users.

The recommended approach is to:

  1. Replicate the manually created users to IAS — either by re-creating them through the SCIM provisioning flow or by synchronizing them into IAS via the appropriate identity provisioning job.
  2. Allow IAS to replicate them back to SSCv2 so that SSCv2 recognizes them as SCIM-managed identities.

Once a user is SCIM-managed, the replication process treats their role assignments as part of the IAS-controlled state. Role assignments will no longer be removed during replication — they will instead be preserved and managed consistently alongside all other provisioned users.

What This Means in Practice

If your SSCv2 tenant is SCIM-enabled, the following rules of thumb apply:

ScenarioRisk
User created manually, roles assigned manuallyHigh — roles will be lost on next replication
User created via SCIM, roles assigned via CIS/IASSafe — roles are managed within the replication loop
User migrated to IAS and replicated back to SSCv2Safe — user is now SCIM-managed

The key principle: in a SCIM-enabled tenant, IAS is the source of truth for role assignments. Any role assignment that exists only in SSCv2 — without a corresponding entry in IAS — is at risk of being overwritten during the next replication cycle.

Recommendations

  • Audit your tenant for manually created users who have business roles assigned. These are the users at risk.
  • Do not mix provisioning strategies for the same set of roles. If a role is managed via SCIM, assume that all assignments for that role will be governed by the IAS replication process.
  • Migrate manually created users to IAS before the next replication run if they need to retain their role assignments.
  • Establish a governance policy that requires all new users in SCIM-enabled tenants to be created through the provisioning pipeline, not manually.
  • Monitor replication logs proactively — the absence of entries in CIS logs does not mean nothing changed in SSCv2.

The Golden Rule: SCIM Is a Day 1 Decision

If SCIM will ever be used in your SSCv2 tenant — even in the future — it must be architected from Day 1.

This is not a configuration preference. It is a foundational architectural decision with production consequences. Here is why:

Scenario RiskLevel Consequence
SCIM enabled before any user creationNoneAll users are provisioned consistently via IAS
SCIM enabled after manual users already existHighFirst replication job silently removes role assignments
Manual users migrated to IAS before next replicationMediumRecoverable — but requires careful, urgent remediation
Manual users NOT migrated before replication runsCriticalUsers lose access in production, no CIS log trace

Even if SCIM is not required at go-live, if there is any possibility it will be introduced later — plan for it now. The cost of retrofitting the provisioning model after manual users are established far exceeds the effort of doing it correctly from the start.

Summary

The loss of role assignments for manually created users in SSCv2 is not a random failure — it is the predictable outcome of a SCIM-enabled tenant architecture where IAS owns the user-role assignment state. The fix requires aligning manually created users with the provisioning model: replicate them to IAS and back to SSCv2, making them SCIM-managed. Once that alignment is in place, the replication process will preserve their role assignments rather than silently remove them.

If you are operating a hybrid environment where both manual and SCIM-provisioned users coexist, this issue is likely already affecting you. Addressing it proactively — before the next replication job runs — is far less disruptive than recovering from unexpected access loss in production.

 

Flow 1: The Problematic Scenario — SCIM Not Planned From Day 1

This is what happens when SCIM is introduced or enabled after users have already been created manually in SSCv2+ESM.

Key Insight: The damage is silent. CIS logs show nothing. The role removal is a side-effect of IAS overwriting SSCv2's local role assignment state — leaving no audit trail pointing to the affected users.

Flow 2: The Correct Approach — SCIM Planned From Day 1

This is the recommended architecture when going to production. SCIM must be the only provisioning channel from the very beginning.

entry.title: Identity and Access Management with Microsoft Entra, Part IV: Integration with SAP Cloud IAG
entry.content:
This scenario extends the architecture introduced in part III by shifting responsibility for provisioning SAP role assignments from SAP Cloud Identity Services (CIS), Identity Provisioning, to SAP Cloud Identity Access Governance (IAG). Microsoft Entra ID Governance manages the access package and its assignment lifecycle, while SAP IAG applies SAP-specific approval workflows, risk controls, and downstream role provisioning. The scenario introduces the new SAP IAG connector in Microsoft Entra and Microsoft Azure Key Vault for securely storing the credential when calling the SAP IAG REST API.

 

Note 📢

Interested in connecting with us and discuss your SAP and Entra scenario? Then join the SAP and Microsoft identity teams at SAP TechEd 2026 in Berlin, and add hands-on session XP263 to your event agenda, where you will learn how SAP Cloud Identity Services, SAP Cloud Identity Access Governance, and Microsoft Entra work together to unify user lifecycle management and governance across SAP and third-party application.

Scenario Overview

The architecture for part IV builds on the identity provisioning scenario introduced in part III of this blog series. Microsoft Entra ID remains the central service ("source of authority", SOA) for identity data, and SAP CIS continues to receive users from Microsoft Entra and provisions them to downstream SAP target systems, such as the SAP system on-premises in the corporate network shown in figure 1.
Figure 1: Scenario Overview

 

However, responsibility for provisioning application access to the SAP backend system changes. In part III, SAP Cloud Identity Services, Identity Provisioning created the backend roles as groups in Microsoft Entra configured as a target system, and translated group memberships provisioned with the Entra SCIM-based SAP CIS provisioning connector into role assignments in the SAP backend system.

In this new scenario, SAP IAG takes over responsibility for governing and provisioning the user’s role assignment to the SAP backend system. Instead of directly translating a Microsoft Entra group assignment into an SAP role assignment, Microsoft Entra now requests access to an SAP IAG business role. SAP IAG processes the access request, applies the configured approval workflow and access controls, and provisions the underlying technical role to the target SAP backend system.
This separation allows each platform to focus on its core capabilities:
  • Microsoft Entra ID Governance provides the entitlement catalogs, access packages, request policies, and the user-facing Microsoft My Access portal.
  • SAP IAG provides SAP business roles, SAP-specific access request workflows, access analysis, risk evaluation, mitigation controls, and provisioning to connected SAP applications in the Cloud and on-premises.
  • SAP CIS maintains the shared user identities and supports identity synchronization between Microsoft Entra and SAP IAG.
  • SAP BTP connectivity service and SAP Cloud Connector provide the technical connection from SAP IAG to the SAP backend system on-premises.
From all components and configurations marked as "new" in figure 1, the SAP IAG tenant is the most important addition to the architecture in this scenario. SAP IAG maintains the business roles that can be requested through Microsoft Entra and maps those business roles to technical roles in connected SAP applications.
In the example scenario, the SAP IAG business role BR_EPM contains the technical role SAP_BC_EPM_DEMO for the SAP ABAP system A4H. This business role is included in a new Microsoft Entra access package SAP EPM IAG and requested by the user Linda Larson. Microsoft Entra does not provision the underlying ABAP role directly. Instead, Microsoft Entra creates an access request in SAP IAG by calling the SAP IAG Access Request Service API. SAP IAG processes the request and, after the configured workflow has completed successfully, provisions the technical role to the target system.
SAP CIS Identity Provisioning remains part of the wider landscape, particularly when SAP IAG connects to supported cloud applications through Identity Provisioning proxy systems. However, SAP IAG now governs the access decision and orchestrates the provisioning operation for the requested SAP business role.
For this integration, Microsoft Entra ID Governance introduces an SAP IAG connector. The connector establishes the integration between Microsoft Entra entitlement management and the SAP IAG tenant. The connector enables administrators to:
  • Add an SAP IAG tenant as a resource to a Microsoft Entra entitlement management catalog
  • Discover SAP IAG business roles
  • Add SAP IAG business roles to Microsoft Entra access packages
  • Create SAP IAG access requests when an access package is assigned
  • Initiate removal requests when an assignment expires or is revoked
  • Retrieve the processing status of SAP IAG access requests
All of the actions above will be executed in the exercises of this blog series scenario. The connector communicates with SAP IAG through the Access Request Service REST APIs and authenticates by using OAuth 2.0 client credentials which require a secure storage option offered by the Azure Key Vault service to store the SAP IAG API OAuth client secret used by the SAP IAG connector. When configuring the connector in Microsoft Entra, the administrator selects the Azure subscription, Key Vault, and secret. The SAP IAG client ID, OAuth token URL, and SAP IAG API URL are configured as additional connector properties coming from the service key created for the SAP IAG API service instance in the SAP BTP subaccount.
 
SAP CIS remains essential to this scenario. Microsoft Entra provisions users to the Identity Directory in the SAP CIS tenant through SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management, RFC 7644). These users and their identifiers are subsequently synchronized into the SAP IAG repository. The Microsoft Entra user's globally unique object ID is mapped to the SAP Global User ID to provide a stable identity correlation across Microsoft Entra, SAP CIS, and SAP IAG. Manager information must also be synchronized when SAP IAG workflows use the user’s manager as an approver. The scenario therefore governs role access for existing users who must already exist in SAP CIS and in the SAP IAG repository before Microsoft Entra submits the SAP IAG access request.
The target SAP applications must be registered and connected to SAP IAG. The provisioning mechanism depends on the application type:
  • For an on-premises system like the SAP Application Server ABAP, SAP IAG uses an SAP BTP destination, the SAP Connectivity service, SAP Cloud Connector, and the required BAPI or RFC interfaces.
  • For supported cloud applications, SAP IAG can use SAP Identity Provisioning proxy systems and the IPS_PROXY destination configured in the BTP subaccount.
The five steps shown in the scenario diagram of figure 1 illustrate the complete access governance process:
  1. Microsoft Entra provisions the users required in SAP IAG (Linda Larson, Tina Johnson & your Entra administrator user) and their SAP IAG roles as group memberships to SAP CIS through the existing enterprise application and SCIM provisioning connection (Note: inbound- or HR-driven provisioning of the test users in this scenario from SAP SuccessFactors to the corporate Active Directory and from there to Entra does not change from the scenario in part III of this blog series). The provisioning configuration must synchronize the Microsoft Entra object ID of the users as the SAP Global User ID. Manager information must also be synchronized if the SAP IAG workflow uses manager-based approval. In this scenario, Tina Johnson is assigned in Active Directory as the manager of Linda Larson and can approve Linda's access request in SAP IAG. After provisioning from Entra to SAP CIS is complete, the relevant SAP IAG synchronization jobs must import the user, groups, and identifiers from SAP CIS into SAP IAG's user repository. All users must be available in SAP IAG before an access request can be submitted from Microsoft Entra.
  2. Linda Larson opens the Microsoft My Access portal and requests the SAP EPM IAG access package. The access package is maintained in a Microsoft Entra entitlement management catalog and contains the SAP IAG business role BR_EPM.
  3. The SAP IAG connector calls the SAP IAG APIs and creates an access request for the user and selected business role. SAP IAG validates the request and that the user exists in its repository.
  4. SAP IAG processes the request according to the workflow and governance configuration of the SAP IAG tenant. Depending on the organization’s configuration, processing can include manager approval, segregation of duties (SOD) analysis, critical access analysis, assignment of mitigation controls and other steps. In this scenario, Tina Johnson as the manager of Linda Larson needs to approve Linda's access request. Microsoft Entra governs eligibility for the access package and its assignment lifecycle. SAP IAG governs the SAP-specific role assignment and applies SAP-specific risk and compliance controls.
  5. After the SAP IAG workflow has completed successfully, SAP IAG provisions the business role to the connected target applications. In the scenario, the business role BR_EPM contains the technical role SAP_BC_EPM_DEMO for the ABAP system A4H. SAP IAG uses the configured SAP BTP destination to reach the target system through SAP Cloud Connector and invokes the required BAPIs. The result is the assignment of SAP_BC_EPM_DEMO to Linda Larson's user in the SAP backend system.

For a live demo, check out episode #307 of the SAP on Azure video podcast, where @Holger-Bruchelt and I go through the scenario step by step.

Microsoft Entra continues to manage the lifecycle of the access package assignment. If the assignment expires or is revoked, Microsoft Entra uses the SAP IAG connector to initiate a removal request. SAP IAG processes that request and deprovisions the corresponding role from the target system. As part of the following exercises, the Microsoft Entra tenant administrator removes Linda's assignment to the SAP EPM IAG access package to test deprovisioning in the scenario.

Prerequisites

Note 📢

This tutorial extends and updates the scenario from part I, part II, and part III. If you arrived here without having completed these three parts of the tutorial series, please do so first, and then come back again.

 
The following additional components and configurations are required to implement SAP IAG-based access governance and role provisioning:
  • An entitlement for the SAP IAG test or standard application plan, and an application subscription to your SAP IAG tenant in the BTP subaccount that is already subscribed to your SAP CIS connectivity plan (see part II) and trusts the SAP CIS tenant as the application identity provider.
  • Administrative access to the SAP IAG tenant with a user assigned to SAP IAG's CIAG_Super_Admin role collection to configure the required settings for this scenario.
  • An entitlement for the SAP IAG standard service plan (technical service name "grc-iag-api"), and a service instance in your BTP subaccount's Cloud Foundry environment to create the service key for accessing your SAP IAG tenant's API with the Entra connector. This is the first step of the following exercises to build the scenario.
  • An Azure subscription with a trust relationship to the Microsoft Entra tenant, and at least administrative access with a user assigned to the Contributor role on a resource group to create the Azure Key Vault instance. The Key Vault stores the SAP IAG API client secret from the service key used by Microsoft Entra to obtain an OAuth access token from SAP BTP to call the SAP IAG API.
  • A new test user Tina Johnson (account name tjohnson) created in the Active Directory (AD) and synchronized to the Cloud with  the Entra Provisioning Agent on-premises and Entra Cloud Sync as described in steps 10.5 to 10.12 of part III. Tina Johnson is the approver of the access request in SAP IAG in this scenario. Linda Larson (account name llarson), who was already on-boarded (steps 9 and 10) in part III, will be used as the user requesting access in this scenario. To make tjohnson the approver in this scenario, she must be assigned as the manager of llarson in AD. Note: You can also test the scenario with users created and managed directly in Entra ID and that do not originate from the on-premises AD. In this case, also make sure that user tjohnson is set as the manager in user llarson's job information profile settings.

Create the SAP IAG API service key

We get started with generating the credentials that are required to authorize the SAP IAG Access Request API calls from the connector in Microsoft Entra.

StepDescriptionScreenshot
1.1

Login to SAP BTP Cockpit and select your subaccount. Navigate to Services → Instances and Subscriptions.
In the list of your subaccount's service instances, click on the ellipsis (•••) of the SAP Cloud Identity Access Governance service instance for the standard plan.

Click Create Service Key from the menu.

1.2

Enter a name for the new service key.

Click Create.

1.3Wait for the completion of the service key operation. Then select it from the list.
1.4

Switch to the Form tab.

Copy and paste the following service key properties to a temporary file:

  • ARQAPI
  • clientid
  • clientsecret
  • url
You will need these values for the configuration of the connector in Entra.
Click Close.

Create the Azure Key Vault

The SAP IAG connector in Entra requires the service key credentials (client id and client secret) to obtain an access token from the SAP BTP Authorization and Trust Management (XSUAA) service to call the SAP IAG tenant's APIs. The connector uses Azure Key Vault to reduces the risk of accidental leaks and ensures that sensitive information like the client secret is stored securely. 

If you already have an Azure Key Vault instance created in your subscription, you can use it in this scenario and jump to step 2.6. Otherwise continue with step 2.1.

StepDescriptionScreenshot
2.1

Login with your Azure administrator account to the Azure Portal.

Click Create a Resource.

2.2

Enter "Key Vault" in the search bar and hit Enter.

On the Key Vault tile in the search results, click Create.

2.3

Select an existing Resource Group or click Create new to create a new one.

Provide a Name (for example "sapiagkv"), select a Region (for example "East US"), and select "Standard" for the Pricing tier.

Keep the other default settings and click Review + create.

2.4Review the Key Vault configuration and click Create.
2.5When the deployment of the new Key Vault is complete, click Go to resource.
2.6

Navigate to Objects → Secrets.

Click Generate/Import.

2.7

Provide a name for new secret (for example "SAPIAGAPIKey"), and copy/paste the value of  clientsecret from step 1.4 into the Secret value field. Make sure you don't have any whitespace characters at the beginning or end of the copied string.

Click Create.

Configure required user attribute mappings

To have a common and globally unique user identifier in this scenario across Microsoft Entra, SAP CIS, and SAP IAG, the user's object id in Entra will be used to fill the following SAP CIS SCIM user attributes:

  • userName
  • externalId
  • urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:sap:2.0:User:userUuid

The last attribute from the list above defines the user's SAP Global User ID which uniquely identifies the user across SAP business applications and services. By filling it with the objectId from the user in Entra we are following the alternative approach as described here and do not rely on SAP CIS to generate the ID in this scenario.

The following step assume that you already have created the enterprise application for the SAP CIS tenant in Microsoft Entra as described in steps 6.1 to 6.23 from part II.

 
StepDescriptionScreenshot
3.1

Login to the Microsoft Entra admin center with your Entra administrator user.

Navigate to Entra ID → Enterprise Applications and select the enterprise application for your SAP CIS tenant from the list.

Select Provisioning from the enterprise application menu.

3.2

Select Attribute mapping from the menu.

On the Users tab, search for the userName target attribute in the list and click the pencil (edit) symbol.

3.3

In the Source attribute (Microsoft Entra ID) drop-down list, select objectId.

Click Apply.

3.4

Repeat steps 3.2 and 3.3 with the following SAP CIS target attributes:

  • externalId
  • urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:sap:2.0:User:userUuid
3.5Verify that the target attribute urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:manager is mapped to the manager source attribute from Microsoft Entra ID.

Create SAP IAG user groups and assign test users

SAP IAG requires a set of specific groups that it looks for when users access the service for administration, workflow approvals, or requesting a business role. Instead of creating these required groups in SAP CIS as described in the SAP IAG admin guide, we create them in Entra and provision them to the SAP CIS tenant with the test users assigned to them.

Note 📢

You only create a subset of the required groups needed for the Access Request service. Other SAP IAG services such as Privileged Access Management are out of scope for this scenario.

 

StepDescriptionScreenshot
4.1

Navigate to Entra ID → Groups.

Click New Group.

4.2

For the Group name, enter IAG_RAA_DEFAULT.

Click Create.

Repeat this step for the following groups:

  • IAG_USER
  • IAG_RCA_DEFAULT
  • IAG_WF_MANAGER
  • IAG_SUPER_ADMIN
4.3

Navigate to Entra ID → Users.

Search for user Linda Larson. If you haven't created this test user (see steps 9 and 10 in part III) yet, please onboard it now either in SAP SuccessFactors, as a new user in Active Directory, or directly in Entra.

Note 📢:  Make sure that the user has an e-mail address configured. If you are using an M365 developer tenant, assign the test user an M365 E5 Developer license in your tenant.

Select Groups from the menu and click Add membership.

4.4

Select the group IAG_USER from the list and click Select.

Repeat steps 4.3 and 4.4 for user Tina Johnson to be the assignment approver in the access request workflow for the business role created in steps 13.x by assigning her the groups IAG_RAA_DEFAULT, IAG_WF_MANAGER and IAG_USER.

Repeat steps 4.3 and 4.4 for user Alex Carter to be the content approver for the business role created in steps 13.x by assigning him the group IAG_RCA_DEFAULT.

Repeat steps 4.3 and 4.4 for your Entra administrator user to be the SAP IAG administrator by assigning this user the group IAG_SUPER_ADMIN.

4.5

Navigate back to Entra ID → Users and search again for user Linda Larson.

On the Overview page, select the Properties tab.

Scroll down to the Job Information category. Check if Tina Johnson is assigned as the Manager.

If not, either set Tina Johnson as the manager directly in the Entra admin center (if they are cloud-only user accounts), or set her as the manager in the Active Directory Users and Computers (ADUC) tool (for on-premises AD user accounts).

Provision SAP IAG groups and users to SAP CIS and SAP ABAP system

The new SAP IAG groups and their assignments to the test users are provisioned to the SAP CIS tenant, and from the tenan's Local Directory with the existing configuration from part II, steps 9.x, in the Identity Provisioning Service (IPS) to the downstream SAP ABAP system A4H.

StepDescriptionScreenshot
5.1

In the Entra admin center, go back to Entra ID → Enterprise Applications and select the enterprise application for your SAP CIS tenant from the list. Select Provisioning from the enterprise application menu.

Select Users and Groups from the provisioning menu, and click Add user/group.

5.2Select None selected.
5.3

Search for "IAG_" and select all groups created in step 4.2 from the search results.

Click Select.

5.4Click Assign.
5.5

Select Provision on demand from the menu.

Search for IAG_RAA_DEFAULT in the Select a user or group field.

Select the group from the search results.

5.6

Select View members only.

From the drop-down list, select Tina Johnson.

Click Provision.

5.7

In the Perform action report you can see that the group and user has been created in the SAP CIS tenant and that the user has been assigned as a member.

Close the report.

Repeat steps 5.5 and 5.6 for group IAG_WF_MANAGER and user Tina Johnson.

Repeat steps 5.5 and 5.6 for group IAG_USER and users Linda Larson and Tina Johnson.

Repeat steps 5.5 and 5.6 for group IAG_RCA_DEFAULT and user Alex Carter.

Repeat steps 5.5 and 5.6 for group IAG_SUPER_ADMIN and your Entra administrator user.

5.8

Login as the administrator to your SAP CIS tenant.

Navigate to Identity Provisioning → Source Systems.

5.9

Select the LocalDirectory source system configured in part II, step 9.4, from the list.

Switch to the Jobs tab.

For the Read Job Type, click Run Now.

5.10

Verify the success provisioning of the new users from the SAP CIS tenant's Local Directory to the SAP ABAP system A4H.

Navigate to Identity Provisioning → Provisioning Logs.

511

Select the most recent job from the list.

From the job Statistics, verify that the user row for the system SAPA4H shows the number users created in SAP ABAP backend system.

Configure Attributes in SAP CIS

Instead of directly assigning the SAP IAG users to the pre-delivered role collections in SAP IAG, we map the previously provisioned SAP IAG groups and memberships in SAP CIS to these role collections. Therefore a new "Groups" attribute must be added to the security token (assertion) issued by SAP CIS to SAP IAG. In addition, the user's first name. last name, and email address with the attribute names defined in the SAP IAG admin guide need to be added.

StepDescriptionScreenshot
6.1

Navigate to Applications & Resources → Applications.

6.2

From the Bundled Applications list, select your SAP BTP subaccount containing the SAP IAG subscription.

Note: If your SAP IAG tenant is listed as a subelement of the SAP BTP subaccount, then select this entry.

Under Trust settings, click on Attributes.

6.3Click Add.
6.4

For the new attribute enter the following values:

  • Name: Groups (with uppercase 'G')
  • Source: Identity Directory
  • Value: All Groups

Repeat steps 6.3 and 6.4 for the following additional attributes required by SAP IAG (Source is always Identity Directory)

  • Name: first_name, Value: First Name
  • Name: last_name, Value: Last Name
  • Name: mail, Value: Email

Click Save.

Map SAP CIS groups to SAP IAG role collections

With the new attributes added to the SAP CIS issued token, we now can map the SAP IAG role collections required for this scenario to the groups. So whenever a user is assigned to any of these groups in Entra, provisioning with the SAP CIS enterprise app synchronizes these entities to SAP CIS, from where SAP IAG receives the token for the user containing the user's group memberships, and SAP IAG provides the authorization with the matching role collection.

StepDescriptionScreenshot
7.1Sign-on to the SAP BTP Cockpit with your BTP administrator and select your BTP subaccount with your SAP IAG tenant's subscription
7.2

Navigate to Security → Role Collections.

From the list of role collections, select CIAG_Display.

7.3

Switch to the User Groups tab.

Click Edit.

7.4

From the Identity Provider drop-down list, select your SAP CIS tenant.

For the group name, enter IAG_USER.

Click Save.

7.5

Repeat steps 7.2 to 7.4 for role collection CIAG_Super_Admin and user group name IAG_SUPER_ADMIN.

Synchronize SAP CIS Users and Groups with SAP IAG

With all user and group information that applies to SAP IAG administration and access request workflows in this scenario stored in the SAP CIS, this content must be synchronized between SAP CIS and SAP IAG through a job called SCI User Group Sync in the SAP IAG tenant.

Note 📢

This step requires that the initial configuration in the SAP BTP subaccount and SAP IAG tenant for the SCI User Group Sync job is already done. Please refer to the detailed instructions in the SAP IAG admin guide to configure the following prerequisites to run the sync job:

  • Create SAP IAG Sync system and secret as the SAP CIS administrator in your SAP CIS tenant
  • Create and configure the destination SAP_Identity_Services_Identity_Directory as the SAP BTP administrator in your SAP BTP subaccount
  • As the SAP IAG administrator, set the Application Parameter for SourceSystem in Configuration Group UserSource to the value SAP_Identity_Services_Identity_Directory in the Configuration app in SAP IAG.

 

StepDescriptionScreenshot
8.1

Open the URL of your SAP IAG tenant in a new browser tab.

You will be prompted to select the identity provider for logon. Choose your SAP CIS tenant from the list.

8.2

Login as the SAP IAG administrator with your Entra administrator user, who is now assigned to the IAG_SUPER_ADMIN group that maps to the CIAG_Super_Admin role collection, to your SAP IAG tenant.

With the Entra tenant being configured as the corporate Identity Provider (see step 1.x and 2.x in part I) in your SAP CIS tenant, login to SAP IAG is delegated to the Entra tenant. 

8.3

From the SAP IAG launchpad, click Job Scheduler.

8.4

Enter a name for the new job and choose Job Category SCI User Group Sync Job.

Click Schedule Job. 

8.5Go back to the Home page in the SAP IAG launchpad and check successful execution of the job by clicking Job History List.
8.6Expand the Job Category SCI User Group Sync Job in the list and check that the Status of your job created in step 8.4 is Completed.

Configure SAP IAG request reason for the integration with Microsoft Entra

The current integration between SAP IAG and Microsoft Entra uses a fixed request reason when Entra creates the access request in SAP IAG. This request reason must be configured in SAP IAG before users start requesting business roles.

StepDescriptionScreenshot
9.1As the Entra and IAG administrator, go back to the Home page of the SAP IAG launchpad, and click Request Reason.
9.2Click Add Request Reason.
9.3

Enter the following values:

  • Name: REQ_REASON_ENTRA_BR
  • Description: for example "Request reason for Microsoft Entra integration"
  • Type: Access Request

Click Save and Activate.

Maintain SAP Cloud Connector settings for integration with SAP IAG

Before creating the business role in SAP IAG containing any roles from the backend, the configuration of the SAP Cloud Connector in part II (see steps 2.x) needs to be enhanced for the integration with SAP IAG.

StepDescriptionScreenshot
10.1

Login to your SAP Cloud Connector instance as the Administrator user. 

Select your BTP subaccount and navigate to Cloud to On-Premises.

Select the virtual host defined for the RFC protocol from the list.

On the Resources table, click Add. 

10.2

Add the following resource to the list:

  • Function Name: SIAG
  • Naming Policy: Prefix

Click Save.

10.3

Add another resource to the list:

  • Function Name: RFC_READ_TABLE
  • Naming Policy: Exact Name

Click Save.

10.4

Verify technical connectivity to the system by clicking check availability.

The Check Result should show Reachable.

Create System user and assign authorizations in SAP ABAP system

To synchronize roles, profiles, and user accounts from the SAP ABAP system into the SAP IAG tenant, a new system user with the required authorizations is required following the instructions from the SAP IAG security guide.
StepDescriptionScreenshot
11.1

Login to your SAP ABAP system as the administrator. 

Execute transaction PFCG for role maintenance to create a new role with the required authorizations.

Chose a name in the Role field, for example ZIAG_PROVISIONING.

Click Single Role.

11.2

Click Save and switch to the Authorizations tab.

Click Change Authorization Data.

11.3Click Do no select templates.
11.4Click Manually to start adding the Authorization Objects.
11.5

Add the following Authorization Objects:

  • S_USER_UID
  • S_RFC
  • S_TCODE
  • S_ADMI_FCD
  • S_TABU_DIS
  • S_TOOLS_EX
  • S_GUI
  • S_USER_AGR

Click Continue (Enter). 

11.6

Repeat step 11.5 for the following Authorization Objects:

  • S_USER_AUT
  • S_USER_GRP
  • S_USER_PRO
  • S_USER_SAS
  • S_USER_SYS
  • S_USER_TCD
  • PLOG
  • S_USER_VAL
  • S_DEVELOP

Configure the Authorization Fields of the added Authorization Objects with the values as documented here.

Note: For Authorization Object S_RFC, also add values SIAG* and RFC_METADATA_GET to Authorization Field RFC_NAME. These two values are required but not listed in the above document.

11.7Click Save, then Generate to create the role profile.
11.8Confirm the generation of the new default profile for your role.
11.9Click Exit.
11.10

Go to user maintenance with transaction code "/nSU01" to create the new system user.

11.11

In the User field, enter "SAPIAG".

Click Create User (F8).

11.12

Enter "SAPIAG" for the Last Name.

Switch to the Logon Data tab.

11.13

Select User Type "System".

Enter a password in New Password, and enter it again in Repeat Password.

Note: You will need the password later for the configuration of the destination SAP IAG uses to access the backend system.

Click Save.

11.14

Switch to the Roles tab.

In first row of the Role Assignments table, enter your new role's name, ZIAG_PROVISIONING.

Click Save.

Create the destination to the SAP ABAP system

For SAP IAG to execute the repository synchronization for the SAP ABAP system, we create a new destination that uses the new system user's credentials from the previous step.

StepDescriptionScreenshot
12.1

Go back to the SAP BTP Cockpit. and navigate to Connectivity → Destinations

Click Create.

12.2Select From Scratch.
12.3

Enter the following Destination Details:

  • Name: SAPA4HIAG
  • Type: RFC
  • Proxy Type: OnPremise
  • Authentication Type: CONFIGURED_USER
  • User: SAPIAG
  • Password: The password entered in step 11.13

Scroll down to Target System Configuration.

12.4

Enter the following target system configuration:

  • Target System Connection Type: Direct Connection
  • Virtual Application Server Host: The virtual host name select in step 10.1, for example sapa4h
  • System Number: The system number of your SAP backend, for example 00
  • Client: The client to use for the connection, for example 001

Scroll down to Pooling Configuration.

12.5

Configure the Pool Capacity for this destination with the value 6, and click the checkbox Pool Check Connection.

Click Save.

Synchronize SAP ABAP identity and authorization data and maintain user mapping

A new application representing the SAP ABAP server must be created in SAP IAG to synchronize roles, profiles and users from the connected backend system. In addition, SAP IAG requires a mapping from the user's master user ID, the Entra object ID used as the SAP Global User ID, to the user's accounts across the different connected systems. For this scenario, Linda Larson's account in the SAP ABAP system must be mapped to successfully provision her role assignment in the system later in step 17.

StepDescriptionScreenshot
13.1Go back to the SAP IAG launchpad Home page and launch Applications.
13.2Click Add.
13.3

Create the new application with the following values:

  • Application name: SAPA4H
  • Description: SAP A4H system
  • Application Type: SAP S/4HANA On-Premise
  • HCP Destination: SAPA4HIAG (the name chosen in step 12.3)

Click Save. 

13.4

Go back to the Home page.

Select Job Scheduler.

13.5

Provide the following configuration for the new job:

  • Job Name: SAPA4H_Sync
  • Job Category: Repository Sync
  • Application Type: SAP S/4HANA On-Premise
  • Application: SAPA4H

Click Schedule Job.

13.6

Gp back to Home page.

Select Job History List.

13.7

Expand the Job Category for Repository Sync and select the Job with the name SAPA4H_Sync.

Check for the Status Completed.

13.8Go back to the Home page of the SAP IAG launchpad and launch User Mapping
13.9Click Create Mapping.
13.10Click the value help for the Master User ID field.
13.11Search for Linda Larson and select her Master User ID from the search results.
13.12

In the Application field, select SAPA4H.

Click on the value help for the Mapped User ID field. 

13.13

Select Linda's local user account in the SAP ABAP System (LLARSON).

Click Create.

Create the business role in SAP IAG

The SAP IAG business role BR_EPM for testing the scenario contains the technical role SAP_BC_EPM_DEMO  from the SAP ABAP system A4H synchronized with the previous step, and the test users provisioned in step 5 are now required to successfully complete the business role creation.

StepDescriptionScreenshot
14.1Go back to the SAP IAG launchpad Home page, switch to the Role Designer tab, and launch Business Roles.
14.2Click Create.
14.3

Enter the following values:

  • Business role: BR_EPM
  • Description: for example "Business Role for the Enterprise Procurement Model (EPM) access"
  • Business process: select GLOBAL Business process

On the Access table, click Add.

14.4

Search for "SAP_BC_EPM_DEMO".

In the search results list, click Add for the EPM Demo Role in application SAPA4H.

14.5

Switch to the Other Attributes tab.

Click the value help on the Content Approvers field.

14.6

Active the checkbox for Alex Carter in the list, who has been assigned to the IAG_RCA_DEFAULT group before.

Click Select.

14.7Click the value help on the Assignment Approvers field.
14.8

Active the checkbox for TIna Johnson in the list, who has been assigned to the IAG_RAA_DEFAULT group before.

Click Select.

14.9

For the Business Subprocess, select GLOBAL Sub Process, and choose Criticality Low.

Click Save and Activate.

Configure Entra IAG Connector

Switching back to Entra now to finalize the scenario setup. Let's get started with connecting the SAP IAG tenant with the new connector in Entra ID Governance Entitlement Management.

StepDescriptionScreenshot
15.1

In the Entra admin center, navigate to ID Governance → Entitlement Management, and select Control configurations from the menu. 

Click View connectors.

15.2Click New connector.
15.3

Enter the following configuration values:

  • Type: SAP IAG
  • Name: A short name for the connector, for example "SAP IAG test tenant"
  • Description: Any text describing your new connector context
  • SubscriptionId: Select the Azure subscription id with the Azure Key Vault configured in steps 2.x
  • Key Vault Name: Select your Key Vault created in steps 2.x from the list
  • Secret Name: Select the secret from your Key Vault configured in step 2.7
  • Client Id: The value for clientidcopied in step 1.4
  • Access Token URL: The value for urlcopied in step 1.4. Add add the suffix /oauth/token to the urlvalue, for example https://myiagtenant.authentication.us20.hana.ondemand.com/oauth/token
  • IAG URL: The value forARQAPIcopied in step 1.4

Click Create.

Create catalog and access package

The final step before the scenario can be testes end-to-end is the creation of the access package containing the business role from IAG that user Linda Larson will request access to.

StepDescriptionScreenshot
16.1

Wait for the new connector to complete the create operation.

Navigate back to Entitlement management.

16.2

Select Catalogs from the menu.

Select the General catalog from the list.

(Note: You can also create a new catalog for the scenario test if needed).

16.3

Select Resources from the menu.

Click Add resources.

16.4Click External Resources (Preview)
16.5

From the Connector drop-down list, select your SAP IAG connector created in step 15.3.

Choose Business Role from the Resource Type drop-down list, and select SAP IAG Access Rights from the available resources for the connector.

Click Select.

16.6

Click Add.

Now any access package in this catalog can contain business roles from SAP IAG.

16.7

Select Access pacakges from the menu.

Click New access package.

16.8

Provide a name (for example SAP EPM IAG) and description for the new access package.

Click Next: Resource roles.

16.9Click External Resources (Preview).
16.10

Select SAP IAG Access Rights from the list of available external resources in the catalog.

Click Select.

16.11

From the Role drop-down list, select the business role BR_EPMcreated in step 14.

Click Next: Request.

16.12

Select For users, service principal, and agent identities in your directory for Who can get access.

Choose All users (including guests) for Select specific scope.

16.13

Scroll down and activate the Self checkbox for Who can request access.

Adjust the following settings:

  • Require requestor justification: No
  • Require approval: No
  • Disable assignment emails: Yes 

Click Next: Requestor Information

16.14

Switch Users can request specific timeline to No, and keep the default settings for all other Lifecycle settings.

Click Next: Rules, then Next: Review + create.

16.15Click Create.
16.16Copy the My Access portal link to the clipboard.

Test the scenario

Ready for testing? You will now go through all steps of the process, starting from requesting the access package as user Linda Larson in the Entra My Access portal, approving the request for the contained business role in SAP IAG as user Tina Johnson, and provisioning the role assignment to the SAP ABAP system as the IAG administrator. 

StepDescriptionScreenshot
17.1

Open a new InPrivate / Incognito window. Paste the link copied in the previous step 16.16.

Login to the My Access portal as user Linda Larson.

17.2

The link automatically selects the newly created access package SAP EPM IAG for the access request.

Click Continue.

17.3You can leave the business justification empty and click Submit request.
17.4

Go back to browser window with the Entra Admin Center from step 16.16.

Navigate to Requests.

Select the new request from the list.

Check that there are no Fulfillment Errors and that the Status is Delivering.

This means that Entra has successfully created the access request in SAP IAG for the business role and is waiting for a workflow status update from SAP IAG. 

17.5Login to SAP IAG as the user Tina Johnson who is the approver in SAP IAG.
17.6Launch Access Request from the SAP IAG launchpad.
17.7Select the new access request created from Entra for Linda Larson from the list.
17.8

Choose Approve.

Click Submit.

17.9

Logout as user Tina Johnson from SAP IAG.

Login to SAP IAG with your Entra administrator user as the SAP IAG admin.

17.10Launch Job Scheduler from the SAP IAG launchpad.
17.11

Enter a Job Name and select Provisioning for the Job Category.

Click Schedule Job.

17.12

Verify successful completion of the new Job by launching Job History List from the SAP IAG launchpad.

Select the Job created in the previous step and check the Job Logs.

Check for an entry that logs the successful assignment of user Linda Larson's local user account in the SAP ABAP system (LLARSON) to the role SAP_BC_EPM_DEMOfrom the business role BR_EPM.

17.13You can also verify the successful role provisioning by logging into the SAP ABAP backend and run transaction SU01 for displaying Linda Larson's role assignments.
17.14Also check the status update of the access package request in Entra. After a few minutes. the status will change from Delivering to Delivered.

As always, hope you enjoyed the scenario, and leave a comment for any feedback or questions.

entry.title: Security Sessions at SAP TechEd Berlin 2026
entry.content:
If you're planning to attend SAP TechEd Berlin (and if you're not planning on going yet, you might want to reconsider after reading this blog!), and you're interested in SAP BTP / SAP BAIP security and identity & access management, this blog is for you. 

Make sure you add these sessions to your agenda, and visit our booth to chat with us - I look forward to seeing you next week!

Security content is bundled under the umbrella of Build Trust in SAP with Security, Compliance, and Identity Management. Let me highlight a few sessions.
